item.title: Discrete four-component massive Thirring model
item.description: arXiv:2611.07686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a discrete four-component massive Thirring model (MTM) within the Cauchy matrix framework. A connection between the dependent variables of the discrete four-component MTM and those of the discrete Mikhailov model is established. Taking two successive continuum limits, we first reduce this discrete four-component MTM to its semi-discrete counterpart, and further arrive at the continuous four-component MTM. Solving the determining equation set enables us to construct AKNS-type and KP-type solutions, including explicit soliton solutions and multiple-pole solutions. Imposing the local reduction and nonlocal reduction on the discrete four-component MTM yields the discrete MTM and the reverse-(n,m) discrete MTM, respectively. For these two reduced systems, we prove that the former admits AKNS-type solutions, whereas the latter possesses both AKNS-type and KP-type solutions.
item.dc:creator: Xiao-gang Mu, Jing Wang, Song-lin Zhao

item.title: The Zhukovskiy-Volterra gyroscope: geometry and reduction
item.description: arXiv:2611.07789v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We describe a symplectic reduction of the Zhukovskiy integrable case of motion of a rigid body about a fixed point with a gyroscope in $\mathbb R^n$ to an integrable magnetic flow on a sphere $S^{n-1}$. We also present Zhukovskiy's geometric interpretation of motion of the Euler top with a gyroscope, aka the Zhukovskiy--Volterra gyroscope, and perform a symplectic reduction of this system to an integrable magnetic flow on a $2$-dimensional sphere.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Dragovi\'c, Borislav Gaji\'c, Bo\v{z}idar Jovanovi\'c

item.title: Universal $x$-$y$ duality in equivariant topological recursion and quartic Kontsevich model
item.description: arXiv:2611.08018v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Topological recursion is a universal procedure that generates an infinite family of multi-differentials with different interpretations in various areas of mathematics. Recently, a new understanding of topological recursion has emerged from $x$-$y$ duality, which relates two such families through explicit formulae. We study $x$-$y$ duality, its parametrised version, and symplectic duality in the setting of equivariant topological recursion. We explicitly analyse the pole structure of the resulting dual families and provide recursive formulae for the different types of polar parts. In contrast to classical topological recursion, the dual family has additional poles at fixed points of the group action, and at anti-diagonals determined by the group action. We show that the partition function $Z_P(E)=\int_{H_N} e^{-N\,\mathrm{Tr}(E\Phi^2+P(\Phi))}d\Phi$ of the Kontsevich matrix model with arbitrary potential $P$, where $d\Phi$ is the Lebesgue measure on Hermitian $N\times N$ matrices and $E$ a positive matrix, admits a Fock space realisation related to the character expansion of the IZHC integral. The Fock space framework provides two mutually $X$-$Y$ dual families of multi-differentials relative to an implicitly defined spectral curve $(X,Y)$. The solution $Y(X)$ succeeds for the quartic Kontsevich model with potential $P(\Phi)=\frac{\lambda}{4}\Phi^4$. We identify a network of duality transformations and symplectic shifts which relate the quartic Kontsevich model with the $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-equivariant spectral curve. The proposed construction yields a conjectural all-genus solution to the quartic Kontsevich model, which reproduces recursive structures previously established for genus $g\leq 1$.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Hock, Jakob Lindner, Raimar Wulkenhaar

item.title: Galois conjugation, droplet growth, and the differential transcendence of the Ising model in nonzero field
item.description: arXiv:2611.08033v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The square-lattice Ising model is exactly solvable in zero magnetic field, but the scope of exact solutions at nonzero field remains unresolved. We show that, at every fixed dimensionless field $H=h/(k_BT)\ne 0$, its free energy and magnetization obey no algebraic differential equation in the coupling $K=J/(k_BT)$. This excludes Onsager-type formulas and broad classes of special-function expressions. Previous work left open a countable set of fields with algebraic-integer fugacities. We eliminate these exceptions using Galois conjugation and the large-order growth of droplets of reversed spins. At conjugate fugacities outside the unit circle, nearly square droplets produce coefficient growth incompatible with an algebraic differential equation. We prove that cancellations cannot remove this growth in the full pressure series. The free-energy result also holds for the Lieb lattice and square lattices with equal-length chain decorations and uniform coupling and field. In every dimension $d\ge2$, we additionally resolve fields for which $e^{-2|H|}$ has a real algebraic conjugate greater than one.
item.dc:creator: Ran Luo, Jiahua Tian

item.title: Oriented V-systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.08326v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the notion of an oriented $\vee$-system which gives a class of solutions of the oriented associativity equations generalising Veselov's $\vee$-system solutions of WDVV equations. An oriented $\vee$-system is a special configuration of pairs of a vector and a covector in a linear space. We show that the class of oriented $\vee$-systems is closed under taking subsystems and restrictions. We provide examples which include a multiparameter family related to imprimitive complex reflection groups.
item.dc:creator: Maali Alkadhem, Misha Feigin

item.title: Elliptic solutions to matrix CKP equation
item.description: arXiv:2608.08774v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A class of elliptic solutions to the matrix CKP equation is studied. Equations of motion for their poles and matrix coefficients at the poles are obtained. As in the scalar case, they are of the first order, in contrast to what takes place in the KP and BKP hierarchies, where the equations of motion are of the second order.
item.dc:creator: A. Zabrodin

item.title: Quantum Kicked Top: A Paradigmatic Model
item.description: arXiv:2604.12345v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The quantum kicked top (QKT) is one of the most widely studied models in quantum chaos, providing a minimal yet powerful framework for exploring the relationship between classical nonlinear dynamics and quantum behavior. Unlike many chaotic systems with infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, the QKT possesses a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, making it analytically and numerically controllable while still showing a rich dynamical phenomena. In this chapter, we present a comprehensive introduction to the QKT as a paradigmatic model of quantum chaos. Starting from the classical kicked top, we derive the discrete nonlinear map governing the dynamics on the unit sphere and analyze its phase space structure through fixed points, stability analysis, bifurcations and Lyapunov exponents. We then discuss the role of symmetries, including rotational and time-reversal symmetry, and how their breaking modifies the dynamics. The quantum description is developed using Floquet theory, where the periodically driven spin system is represented by a unitary Floquet operator acting on a $(2j+1)$-dimensional Hilbert space. Within this framework, signatures of quantum chaos such as spectral statistics, entanglement generation and recurrences are discussed. The model also admits an interpretation as a system of interacting qubits, enabling explicit few-qubit realizations and direct connections with quantum information measures through reduced density matrices and entanglement entropy. By linking classical phase space structures with quantum dynamical indicators, the QKT provides a clear setting to investigate the emergence of chaotic behavior in the semiclassical limit. The chapter, therefore, highlights the quantum kicked top as a bridge between nonlinear classical dynamics, quantum chaos and modern quantum information science.
item.dc:creator: Avadhut V. Purohit, Udaysinh T. Bhosale
